title: Android update safety: stable release signing, CI fingerprint guard and CSV import/restore - V-model spec suite
derived_from: Locked decisions D-A..D-E from discussion #259 (owner-confirmed 2026-11-14 with security hardening) plus tracking issue #258 (SSOT, acceptance criteria and scope IN/OUT) - documentation only, zero new decisions (Stage 2 rule)

requirements.text: Release APK builds SHALL be signed with the stable release certificate: the release signingConfig SHALL read the gitignored android/keystore.properties or the DKBT_RELEASE_* environment variables and SHALL fail the build with a named error when neither is configured.

acceptance_criteria.given: android/keystore.properties exists and points at release.jks
acceptance_criteria.then: the produced APK is signed with the release certificate referenced in the properties file

acceptance_criteria.given: DKBT_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_FILE, DKBT_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, DKBT_RELEASE_KEY_ALIAS and DKBT_RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD are set instead
acceptance_criteria.then: the produced APK is signed with the certificate material from the environment

acceptance_criteria.given: neither keystore.properties nor the DKBT_RELEASE_* variables are configured
acceptance_criteria.then: the build fails with the named 'Release signing is not configured' GradleException

requirements.text: Debug builds SHALL continue to sign with the default debug keystore and SHALL NOT require any release signing material.

acceptance_criteria.given: no keystore.properties and no DKBT_RELEASE_* variables exist
acceptance_criteria.then: the build succeeds and the APK carries the debug keystore signature

acceptance_criteria.given: release signing material is fully configured
acceptance_criteria.then: the debug APK is still signed with the debug keystore, not the release certificate

requirements.text: The release-tagged CI workflow SHALL source all signing material from GitHub Actions secrets in a protected environment, SHALL NOT read any committed key file, and fork-triggered runs SHALL NOT receive the secrets.

acceptance_criteria.given: the repository secrets are configured in the protected environment
acceptance_criteria.then: the workflow decodes the keystore secret to a runner-local file and exports the DKBT_RELEASE_* variables from secrets only

acceptance_criteria.given: any *.jks, *.keystore or keystore.properties file is tracked in git
acceptance_criteria.then: the scan fails and names the tracked file

acceptance_criteria.given: a fork pull request triggers CI
acceptance_criteria.then: the secrets are absent and the build falls back to debug signing without touching release material

requirements.text: The release signing workflow SHALL trigger only on protected release tags (v*) and the signing environment SHALL require a reviewer before secrets are exposed to a job.

acceptance_criteria.given: a push to a non-tag branch
acceptance_criteria.then: the release signing job does not run

acceptance_criteria.given: a release tag push starts the workflow
acceptance_criteria.then: the job waits for the configured reviewer approval before the signing secrets are exposed

requirements.text: After building a release APK, CI SHALL extract the signer certificate fingerprint with apksigner verify --print-certs and SHALL fail the job when the SHA-256 fingerprint does not match the pinned release fingerprint.

acceptance_criteria.given: a release APK signed with release.jks
acceptance_criteria.then: the extracted SHA-256 fingerprint equals the pinned value and the job passes

acceptance_criteria.given: a release APK signed with any other key (for example a debug key)
acceptance_criteria.then: the job fails and the mismatch is named in the log

requirements.text: The fingerprint guard SHALL skip with a visible annotation instead of failing when the pinned fingerprint or keystore secret is absent (fork/PR and development CI).

acceptance_criteria.given: no pinned-fingerprint secret is configured
acceptance_criteria.then: it exits 0 and prints a visible skip annotation

acceptance_criteria.given: a development CI run without release material
acceptance_criteria.then: the guard did not block the run

requirements.text: The app SHALL provide a CSV import/restore route that accepts exactly the machine backup format emitted by /export.csv?scope=backup and SHALL cover every column that the backup export emits.

acceptance_criteria.given: a backup export file from /export.csv?scope=backup
acceptance_criteria.when: it is submitted to the import route
acceptance_criteria.then: every column the backup exporter emits is accepted and mapped to the restore target

acceptance_criteria.given: a CSV with an unknown extra column or a missing required column
acceptance_criteria.then: the import is rejected with a named error that names the offending column

requirements.text: Importing a backup CSV SHALL restore the ledger into the local SQLite database so that export, import into a fresh database and re-export round-trips to an equivalent ledger, and a repeated import SHALL be refused instead of duplicating rows.

acceptance_criteria.given: a seeded database with bonds, payments and goals
acceptance_criteria.when: the backup CSV is exported, imported into a fresh database and re-exported
acceptance_criteria.then: the first and second exports are equal

acceptance_criteria.given: the same import file is submitted twice in a row against the same database
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused with a clear already-restored or duplicate error and no rows are duplicated

requirements.text: Import SHALL be an explicit, user-driven action in the Settings UI with clear feedback and SHALL never run silently or automatically.

acceptance_criteria.given: the Settings page
acceptance_criteria.then: an import/restore entry point is visible with a warning that it restores ledger data

acceptance_criteria.given: a successful import
acceptance_criteria.then: the UI shows the counts of imported bonds, payments and goals

acceptance_criteria.given: a failed import
acceptance_criteria.then: the UI shows the named error and the ledger state is unchanged

requirements.text: Import SHALL validate before writing and SHALL apply the restore atomically: a malformed file, wrong scope or constraint violation leaves the ledger unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.given: a CSV containing one broken row (bad date or non-numeric amount)
acceptance_criteria.then: it aborts with the offending row number named and no rows are written

acceptance_criteria.given: a valid backup CSV
acceptance_criteria.then: all rows are committed in a single transaction

requirements.text: The release-note template SHALL state the signing model and the one-time migration flow and SHALL NOT present data-destroying updates as a caveat.

acceptance_criteria.given: the release-note template
acceptance_criteria.then: both the signing model and the export-uninstall-install-import migration flow appear

acceptance_criteria.given: the repository docs and templates
acceptance_criteria.when: they are scanned for caveat wording that normalises update data loss
acceptance_criteria.then: no such wording remains

requirements.text: The About page SHALL document the update and migration flow for debug-era installs before v1.0.8 ships.

acceptance_criteria.given: the About page
acceptance_criteria.then: it contains the export, uninstall, install, import flow for users coming from a debug-signed install

requirements.text: android/SIGNING.md SHALL carry a key-leak response section and key-backup guidance, and SHALL state the 25+ year key validity guidance.

acceptance_criteria.given: android/SIGNING.md
acceptance_criteria.then: the key-leak response section and the key-backup guidance section both exist

acceptance_criteria.given: the keytool generation instructions
acceptance_criteria.then: they include the 25+ year validity guidance

prd_items.statement: Release APK builds SHALL be signed with the stable release certificate: the release signingConfig SHALL read the gitignored android/keystore.properties or the DKBT_RELEASE_* environment variables and SHALL fail the build with a named error when neither is configured.
Debug builds SHALL continue to sign with the default debug keystore and SHALL NOT require any release signing material.

The release-tagged CI workflow SHALL source all signing material from GitHub Actions secrets in a protected environment (keystore as a base64 secret decoded at run time, passwords as secret environment variables), SHALL NOT read any committed key file, and fork-triggered runs SHALL NOT receive the secrets.
The release signing workflow SHALL trigger only on protected release tags (v*) and the signing environment SHALL require a reviewer before secrets are exposed to a job.

After building a release APK, CI SHALL extract the signer certificate fingerprint with apksigner verify --print-certs and SHALL fail the job when the SHA-256 fingerprint does not match the pinned release fingerprint.
The fingerprint guard SHALL skip with a visible annotation instead of failing when the pinned fingerprint or keystore secret is absent (fork/PR and development CI).
The app SHALL provide a CSV import/restore route that accepts exactly the machine backup format emitted by /export.csv?scope=backup and SHALL cover every column that the backup export emits.

Importing a backup CSV SHALL restore the ledger into the local SQLite database so that export, import into a fresh database and re-export round-trips to an equivalent ledger, and a repeated import SHALL be refused instead of duplicating rows.
Import SHALL be an explicit, user-driven action in the Settings UI with clear feedback (success counts or the named error) and SHALL never run silently or automatically.
Import SHALL validate before writing and SHALL apply the restore atomically: a malformed file, wrong scope or constraint violation leaves the ledger unchanged.
The release-note template SHALL state the signing model and the one-time migration flow (export, uninstall, install, import) and SHALL NOT present data-destroying updates as a caveat.
The About page SHALL document the update and migration flow for debug-era installs before v1.0.8 ships.

android/SIGNING.md SHALL carry a key-leak response section (theft consequences, no revocation, package-name-change escape) and key-backup guidance (offline copy, password manager, losing the key is as fatal as leaking it), and SHALL state the 25+ year key validity guidance.

test_cases.title: Release signingConfig wiring and fail-loud (US-01)
test_cases.steps: 1. Parse android/app/build.gradle. 2. Assert the release signingConfig reads keystore.properties and the DKBT_RELEASE_* environment variables. 3. Assert the missing-both path raises the named GradleException.
test_cases.expected: Release config wired from properties or environment; fail-loud error present

test_cases.title: Debug builds unaffected (US-02)
test_cases.steps: 1. Assert the debug build type does not reference signingConfigs.release. 2. Assert assembleDebug needs no release material.
test_cases.expected: Debug signing stays on the default debug keystore regardless of release material

test_cases.title: Secrets-only signing material in CI (US-03)
test_cases.steps: 1. Parse .github/workflows/android-build.yml. 2. Assert signing inputs come from secrets and the keystore is decoded at run time. 3. Assert no tracked file under android/ matches *.jks, *.keystore or keystore.properties.
test_cases.expected: All signing material flows from secrets; zero committed key material

test_cases.title: Release trigger and environment protection (US-04)
test_cases.steps: 1. Parse the release workflow trigger. 2. Assert it fires only on v* tags. 3. Assert the signing environment is declared and protected.
test_cases.expected: Release signing runs only on protected release tags behind a gated environment

test_cases.title: Fingerprint guard accepts release key, rejects others (CG-01)
test_cases.steps: 1. Build the release APK. 2. Run apksigner verify --print-certs and extract the SHA-256 fingerprint. 3. Compare with the pinned secret. 4. Repeat with a debug-signed APK.
test_cases.expected: Match passes; mismatch fails the job naming the mismatch

test_cases.title: Guard skip path without secrets (CG-02)
test_cases.steps: 1. Run the guard with the fingerprint secret unset. 2. Assert exit code 0 and the skip annotation in the output.
test_cases.expected: Guard skips visibly without breaking the run

test_cases.title: Import covers every exported column (IR-01)
test_cases.steps: 1. Seed a database. 2. Export /export.csv?scope=backup. 3. Submit the file to the import route. 4. Assert every emitted column is accepted. 5. Submit a file with an extra unknown column and one with a missing column.
test_cases.expected: Full column coverage; unknown/missing columns rejected with named errors

test_cases.title: Export-import-export round trip and duplicate refusal (IR-02)
test_cases.steps: 1. Seed a database with bonds, payments and goals. 2. Export the backup CSV (scope=backup). 3. Import into a fresh database. 4. Re-export. 5. Compare the two exports. 6. Import the same file again into the restored database.
test_cases.expected: Exports equal after round trip; second import refused without duplication

test_cases.title: Settings import entry point and feedback (IR-03)
test_cases.steps: 1. Render Settings. 2. Assert the import/restore entry point with its warning. 3. Run a successful import and check the counts feedback. 4. Run a failing import and check the named error and unchanged ledger.
test_cases.expected: Explicit UI entry point; success counts; failure names the error and changes nothing

test_cases.title: Import validation and atomic restore (IR-04)
test_cases.steps: 1. Submit a backup CSV with one broken row and assert abort with the row number and zero writes. 2. Submit a valid CSV and assert a single-transaction commit.
test_cases.expected: Malformed input aborts cleanly; valid input commits atomically

test_cases.title: Release notes state model and migration, no caveat (DOC-01)
test_cases.steps: 1. Read the release-note template. 2. Assert the signing model and migration flow are present. 3. Scan docs and templates for caveat wording that normalises update data loss.
test_cases.expected: Template carries the model and flow; no caveat wording remains

test_cases.title: About page migration flow (DOC-02)
test_cases.steps: 1. Render the About page. 2. Assert the export-uninstall-install-import flow is documented for debug-era installs.

test_cases.title: SIGNING.md leak response and backup guidance (DOC-03)
test_cases.steps: 1. Read android/SIGNING.md. 2. Assert the key-leak response section and the key-backup guidance exist. 3. Assert the 25+ year validity guidance in the keytool instructions.
test_cases.expected: Leak response, backup guidance and validity guidance all present

changelog.note: First suite from locked discussion #259: US-01..US-04 (stable signing + CI secrets + tag/environment hardening), CG-01..CG-02 (fingerprint guard + skip path), IR-01..IR-04 (CSV import/restore round trip, UI entry, atomic restore), DOC-01..DOC-03 (release notes, About, SIGNING.md leak/backup). 13 requirements, 13 tests, full bindings.

AMENDMENT (PM decision, owner-delegated full authority): W1's implementation dialog revealed the scope=full view export lacks bond details (start_date/tenure/credit_day) and goals, pinned by 3 tests - the round-trip cannot bind to it. IR-01/IR-02 + TC-IR-01/TC-IR-02 now bind the restore round-trip to a NEW machine backup export /export.csv?scope=backup (complete bond fields + payments + goals, Settings download button); /export.csv?scope=full and its pinned tests stay unchanged. Supersede-style: no prior confirmed text rewritten outside these IR entries.
R1 gate-3 F-2 fix: IR-04's remaining 'full-ledger CSV' given-clause aligned to the backup CSV naming (v1.1 amendment follow-through); TC-IR-04 steps aligned.
